Text: Java has {{c1::8}} primitive types.
Extra: They are byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, and boolean.

Text: The 8 primitive types are {{c1::byte}}, {{c2::short}}, {{c3::int}}, {{c4::long}}, {{c5::float}}, {{c6::double}}, {{c7::char}}, and {{c8::boolean}}.
Extra: This is worth memorizing exactly.

Text: The default type for integer literals is {{c1::int}}.
Extra: Use `L` for long literals when needed.

Text: The default type for decimal literals is {{c1::double}}.
Extra: Use `F` for float literals.

Text: Primitive types store {{c1::values directly}}, while reference types store {{c2::references to objects}}.
Extra: This is the core mental model for data types.

Text: `String` is a {{c1::reference type}}, not a primitive type.
Extra: String has special syntax but is still an object type.

Text: {{c1::Widening}} casting converts a smaller compatible type to a larger type, while {{c2::narrowing}} casting converts a larger type to a smaller type.
Extra: Narrowing may lose data.

Text: {{c1::Autoboxing}} converts a primitive to a wrapper, while {{c2::unboxing}} converts a wrapper to a primitive.
Extra: Example: `int` <-> `Integer`.

Text: The wrapper class for `int` is {{c1::Integer}}.
Extra: Wrappers are needed for collections and generics.

Text: Calling a method on {{c1::null}} can cause `NullPointerException`.
Extra: Null means no object reference.

Text: For primitives, `==` compares {{c1::values}}; for objects, `==` compares {{c2::references}}.
Extra: Use `.equals()` for many object content comparisons.

Text: String content should usually be compared with {{c1::.equals()}} instead of {{c2::==}}.
Extra: This is a common interview and beginner bug topic.

Text: `int` is the default type for {{c1::integer}} literals.
Extra: Example: `10` is an int literal by default.

Text: `double` is the default type for {{c1::decimal}} literals.
Extra: Example: `9.99` is double by default.

Text: A `long` literal commonly uses suffix {{c1::L}}.
Extra: Prefer uppercase `L`.

Text: A `float` literal commonly uses suffix {{c1::F}}.
Extra: Without `F`, decimal literals are double.

Text: `char` literals use {{c1::single quotes}}, while `String` literals use {{c2::double quotes}}.
Extra: Example: `'A'` vs `"A"`.

Text: Java booleans can only be {{c1::true}} or {{c2::false}}.
Extra: Java does not use 0/1 as booleans.

Text: Local variables must be {{c1::assigned before use}}.
Extra: Fields have default values, local variables do not.

Text: Calling a method on `null` can cause {{c1::NullPointerException}}.
Extra: There is no object to receive the method call.

Text: In integer division, `5 / 2` evaluates to {{c1::2}}.
Extra: Both operands are integers.

Text: In floating-point division, `5 / 2.0` evaluates to {{c1::2.5}}.
Extra: At least one operand is floating-point.

Text: Arithmetic on `byte` values is promoted to {{c1::int}}.
Extra: This is why `byte c = a + b` can fail.

Text: The wrapper class for `boolean` is {{c1::Boolean}}.
Extra: Wrapper classes are object versions of primitives.

Text: The wrapper class for `char` is {{c1::Character}}.
Extra: Not `Char`.

Text: `List<int>` is invalid because generics require {{c1::reference types}}.
Extra: Use `List<Integer>`.

Text: Unboxing {{c1::null}} causes `NullPointerException`.
Extra: Example: `Integer x = null; int y = x;`.
